case_name: Naresh Kumar vs Ut Of J&K & Anr

parties.respondent_defendant: Ut Of J&K & Anr (wife) and another

facts_of_case: The parties have settled their disputes amicably and want the FIR quashed. The petitioner claims the FIR is false and frivolous, and that the respondent married him while concealing her earlier existing marriage.

legal_principles.principle: The power to quash under Section 482 is attracted even if the offence is non-compoundable.
legal_principles.held: The power to quash under Section 482 is attracted even if the offence is non-compoundable.
cited_cases: Parbatbhai Aahir Alias Parbatbhai Bhimsinhbhai Karmur and Ors vs State of Gujarat and Anr. (2017) 9 SCC 641
use_in: case type 1: quashing FIR or criminal proceedings
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — important principle for invoking court's extraordinary powers

legal_principles.principle: The invocation of the jurisdiction of the High Court to quash a First Information Report or a criminal proceeding on the ground that a settlement has been arrived at between the offender and the victim is not the same as the invocation of jurisdiction for the purpose of compounding an offence.
legal_principles.held: While the invocation of the jurisdiction for the purpose of compounding an offence is governed by the provisions of Section 320 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the power to quash under Section 482 is attracted even if the offence is non-compoundable.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 — Sections 320 and 482
cited_cases: Parbatbhai Aahir Alias Parbatbhai Bhimsinhbhai Karmur and Ors vs State of Gujarat and Anr. (2017) 9 SCC 641
use_in: case type 2: quashing FIR or criminal proceedings due to settlement between parties
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — important distinction between compounding and quashing

outcome.final_order: The Court has accepted the compromise deeds and quashed the FIR.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for quashment of FIR
